nodes.title: Generalized Tate n-gons
nodes.statement: For n≥1 put A=ℤ[[t]], q=tⁿ. Glue the n formal node charts A{Xᵢ,Yᵢ}/(XᵢYᵢ−t), i∈ℤ/n, along their punctured branches to a proper formal n-gon; the identifications match consecutive branches and preserve the sections (1,t). Algebraize with the ample rotation orbit of these sections. The resulting generalized elliptic curve Tateₙ(t)/A has split n-gon fibre at t=0, smooth elliptic generic locus t≠0, degeneracy ideal (t), and canonical identity-component formal group Ĝₘ. Its generic elliptic curve is Tate₁(q), with the comparison fixed at the identity. This adds the generalized proper family to the existing equation-level Tate curve, not new coefficients.
hypotheses: No inversion of 2, 3 or n; a node has complete local equation XY=t.
The conventional Weierstrass coefficients and Laurent-series ellipticity already exist in current Tau Ceti; the construction is the proper generalized family.

sources.match: The glued formal family, ample rotation divisor, algebraization and uniqueness give the generalized n-gon extension.

proofSteps: Glue node charts with the cyclic branch identification from Conrad §2.5; compare the formal smooth locus to Ĝₘ and the rotation action.
Use the supplied polarized formal algebraization and full faithfulness to algebraize the curve and action.
Apply the Deligne–Rapoport structure criterion imported from R13.1; Theorem 2.5.2 identifies the generic Tate curve and makes the identity comparison unique.
acceptance: n=1 specializes to the pointed nodal cubic; n=2 has two rational components and two nodes.
The generic invariant satisfies j=q⁻¹+744+O(q), hence pole order n in t.

nodes.title: Power isogenies at the boundary
nodes.statement: For m,n≥1 the branch power maps give a pointed finite morphism Tateₙ(t)→Tateₙ(tᵐ) of generic degree m. Its restriction to the smooth loci is finite locally free of rank m, with kernel μₘ in the identity component and pullback du/u↦m du/u. The proper morphism is not flat at the nodes for m>1: over a field, the completed target-to-source map is k[[t,X,Y]]/(XY−tᵐ) → k[[t,x,y]]/(xy−t), X↦xᵐ, Y↦yᵐ, and the fibre at the closed target node is k[x,y]/(xy,xᵐ,yᵐ) of length 2m−1. The target is the base change t↦tᵐ of the n-gon family and need not have regular total space. On generic fibres the map is u↦uᵐ from Tate₁(tⁿ) to Tate₁(tⁿᵐ).

sources.match: The displayed branch maps and smooth-locus isogeny are used with the finite-flat assertion on the whole proper curve corrected by source issue E307. The finite-flat moduli maps of Theorem 4.4.3 are different morphisms.

proofSteps: Raise branch coordinates to the mth power, respecting the overlap and equations xy=t and XY=tᵐ. Each branch coordinate is integral over its mth power, so these charts give a finite map.

Use SF.4 algebraization and full faithfulness for the proper formal maps. Generic degree m follows from the elliptic isogeny; smooth-locus flatness follows from the μₘ torsor on Gₘ, component by component.

At a target node set t=X=Y=0. The remaining monomials 1,x,…,x^(m−1),y,…,y^(m−1) form a basis of the fibre, giving length 2m−1. A finite flat map of generic rank m would have fibre length m, so the proper map is not flat for m>1.
The smooth-locus power map gives the kernel and differential, including the zero differential in characteristic dividing m.
acceptance: For m=p in characteristic p the generic isogeny is inseparable of degree p, the smooth-locus kernel has rank p and the differential vanishes; this does not imply flatness of the proper power map.
For m=2 the target-node fibre has length 3, whereas the generic degree is 2. Reject a finite-flat assertion for the whole proper morphism.

nodes.title: Formal level structures at cusps
nodes.statement: For a specified Γ-level problem, form its finite generic level cover on Tate₁(q) and take the integral closure of the q-adic base in each generic component. Classify the boundary data on split n-gons via their smooth locus Gₘ×ℤ/n and Drinfeld generators, keeping the stabilizer action on the smoothing parameter and Hodge line. The resulting formal stack charts, with their descent groupoids, describe the completion of the compactified stack. A complete local ring of its coarse curve is an invariant ring only under the applicable coarse-completion theorem; it is not the framed stack chart itself. On the prime N≥5 diamond class over ℤ[1/N], use Layer 10’s existing cusp charts and prove comparison with this generalized family.

nodes.title: Integral Γ₁ cusp strata
nodes.statement: For d|N let B_d be the d-gon boundary stratum of the Γ₁(N) stack. It is reduced, regular, proper, quasi-finite and flat of relative dimension zero over ℤ. If d>2, it is a disjoint union of φ(d)/2 copies of Spec ℤ[ζ_(N/d)], indexed by b∈(ℤ/d)×/{±1}. Its geometric generic degree is φ(d)φ(N/d)/2. A primitive root ζ_(N/d)^r, r a unit modulo N/d, labels a geometric embedding within that cyclotomic component, not an additional component indexed by a positive divisor of d. This corrects the author PDF’s component indexing in Theorem 4.3.4. If d≤2, the stratum is nowhere a scheme for (N,d)=(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(4,2). In the remaining partial schematic cases N=pˢ or 2pˢ the required inversion is δ=p; in other cases δ=1. The canonical degree-two cover by Spec ℤ[ζ_(N/d)] remains finite flat without that inversion; on the schematic locus over ℤ[1/δ] it is Spec(ℤ[ζ_(N/d)]⁺[1/δ]). The same covers extend to every infinitesimal boundary neighbourhood. Do not erase the residual inertia in a nowhere-schematic case.

sources.match: Use the schematic locus and degree-two covers with the exceptional small levels; correct the d>2 component indexing by the isomorphism calculation in the proof, rather than the overcount in the printed statement.

proofSteps: In characteristic zero write a point as (ζ_N^r,b), with b a unit modulo d and r a unit modulo N/d. The μ_d automorphisms change r by (N/d)b times an integer, leaving r modulo N/d; inversion sends (r,b) to (−r,−b). For d>2 it acts freely on b. Cyclotomic Galois action is transitive on r modulo N/d, so there is one cyclotomic component per b modulo sign. Normality and finite flatness extend this decomposition integrally.
Use the twisted Tate charts for existence and the completed moduli property for the full infinitesimal claim.
Descend the degree-two cover only on the stated schematic locus.
acceptance: N=4,d=2 has a non-schematic boundary stratum; taking its real cyclotomic ring does not turn it into a fine moduli scheme.
For d>2 each cyclotomic chart is a scheme even at primes dividing N.

nodes.title: Twisted Tate charts for Γ₁
nodes.statement: For d|N and a unit r modulo N/d, the unmarked regularized Tate curve over ℤ[ζ_(N/d)][[t]], t=q^(1/d), has generic parameter ζ_(N/d)^(−r)q and boundary ideal (t); over ℤ[ζ_N] it is Tate_d(ζ_N^(−r′)t), for any lift r′ modulo N. For a marked Γ₁ chart choose b a unit modulo d and a unit lift b′ modulo N. The point denoted q^(b/d) descends from Tate_d(ζ_N^(−r′(b′)⁻¹)t) to the regularized family with generic parameter ζ_(N/d)^(−r(b′)⁻¹)q. For d>2 this identifies the completion of the component indexed by b modulo sign. The unit r changes its cyclotomic embedding, not its component count; impose no purported unique positive-divisor lift of r. For d≤2 retain the finite flat degree-two formal cover; when N/d>2 it is étale only after inverting δ. For d=2, after inverting δ on the schematic locus, the invariant parameter is (1+ζ_(N/d)⁻¹)t, as in Theorem 4.3.7, rather than an unqualified parameter t on the real base.

nodes.title: Boundary carriers and Hodge evaluation
nodes.statement: On each stated integral stack chart the boundary is an effective relative Cartier divisor cut out by its smoothing parameter, and ω=e*Ω¹ of the smooth locus agrees with the pushforward of the relative dualizing line. It is trivialized on Tate charts by du/u, invariant under contraction. A weight-k section evaluates as a formal series times (du/u)^k, equivariantly for chart stabilizers; restriction of global sections is injective whenever the chosen union of formal boundary charts meets every irreducible component and the sheaf has the required torsion-free/density property. This is the formal comparison supporting the q-expansion principle; one-cusp integral descent is a separate R15 input. Distinguish the Cartier boundary, its reduced boundary locus and the finite-flat scheme j⁻¹(∞), whose ramification multiplicities are cusp widths. For general Γ₀ integral coarse spaces use the Cartier and regular-cusp theorem below; finite flatness of a reduced coarse cusp locus over ℤ is not inferred.

nodes.title: Integral coarse modular curves
nodes.statement: For an open H≤GL₂(Ẑ) containing Γ(n), take the finite-inertia coarse space X_H of the corresponding compactified level stack 𝒳_H (R13.4a/deligne-rapoport-level-stack; for the full, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ levels it is R13.2's moduli stack, by R13.4a/standard-level-stack-identifications). It is a projective normal ℤ-scheme, finite locally free over ℙ¹_j and flat of relative dimension one. The construction is algebraic: normalize the j-line in the generic level algebra and compare the stack coarse space to this normalization. Full level has its determinant/cyclotomic constant algebra, fixed-pairing level is over the corresponding cyclotomic integer base, Γ₁ is the marked-generator problem, and Γ₀ uses the refined cyclic-subgroup stack. Keep disconnected full-level generic components in the normalization algebra. No analytic connectedness or R12.6 is used.

nodes.statement: On the elliptic locus X_H agrees with the affine coarse moduli scheme from ModularCurves 9D, by equality of the moduli problem and its categorical coarse property. nodes.statement: For every N≥1, the integral Γ₀(N) coarse curve is regular at every cusp, including residue characteristics 2 and 3. nodes.title: The cyclic modular polynomial
nodes.statement: For m≥2 define Φ_m(U,V) by the generic cyclic degree-m quotient of the universal j-elliptic curve: its roots in V are j(E/C) for cyclic subgroups C of order m. This gives the irreducible polynomial in ℤ[U,V], monic of degree ψ(m)=m∏_(p|m)(1+1/p) in each variable, symmetric in U,V. Set Φ₁(U,V)=V−U with this orientation. The map (j,j′) from Y₀(m)_ℚ is finite birational onto the plane curve Φ_m=0, and ℚ(X₀(m))=ℚ(j,j′); the smooth coarse curve is its normalization. The integral plane image is not asserted to be the normal integral modular curve, nor does this normalization commute with arbitrary reduction. Cyclic degree ψ(m) differs from the full-subgroup Hecke degree σ₁(m).

nodes.title: Projective scalar level quotients
nodes.statement: For prime p>3 over ℤ[1/p], form the coarse quotient of honest full level p by scalar change of frame a∈𝔽_p×. It classifies a torsion framing modulo scalar up to isomorphism, as a coarse moduli space. The element [−1] remains an automorphism of the unrigidified projective-frame stack, so this quotient is not a fine moduli scheme carrying a descended universal curve. Over ℂ it has two components indexed by the square class of the determinant/Weil pairing; PGL₂(𝔽_p) exchanges these when the determinant is nonsquare, and PSL₂ fixes each. On the p-gon compactification, distinguish full raw stabilizers from the effective rigidification by [−1]; the effective ramification orders over the j-line are 2,3,p. The p-gon automorphism and torsion carriers themselves are imported from R13.1.

nodes.title: The split Cartan normalizer quotient
nodes.statement: For a prime ℓ, over ℚ there is an algebraic isomorphism X₀(ℓ²)/⟨w_(ℓ²)⟩≃X_s(ℓ), where X_s denotes the normalizer of split Cartan, or equivalently the moduli of an unordered pair of distinct ℓ-subgroups. Given a cyclic chain E→E/C_ℓ→E/C_(ℓ²), the middle curve has two distinct order-ℓ subgroups, one from the dual first isogeny and the other from the second; reversing the chain exchanges the pair. The inverse construction and finite-normal compactification comparison establish the isomorphism. This is not the ordered split-Cartan curve. At ℓ itself it is a generic-fibre identification; the semistable quotient is constructed after the explicit extension in R13.5.

nodes.statement: For every prime p and n≥1, the normalized Tate Γ₀(pⁿ) cover of ℤ[[q]] is the disjoint union of ℤ[[q]], ℤ[[s]] with q=s^(pⁿ), and, for a+b=n with a,b>0, the following rings: if a≥b, ℤ[ζ_(pᵇ)][[q]]; if b>a, ℤ[ζ_(pᵃ)][[q]][z]/(z^(p^(b−a))−ζ_(pᵃ)q). These are q-adically complete finite rings, each regular. The generic mixed component comes from the cyclotomic condition Φ_p(z^(p^(b−1))/q^(p^(a−1)))=0 before normalization. For Γ₀(pⁿM), p∤M, factor the generic level cover, tensor with the prime-to-p cusp cover and normalize; the tensor product before normalization need not be normal. This is a composite/bad-level extension; prime-level rings after inverting p remain Layer 10’s.

nodes.title: Generic components and cusp fields
nodes.statement: After the algebraic construction, use R12.3/R12.6 to identify each generic-fibre component of X_H with the compactified analytic quotient for its determinant orbit. For honest full level n over ℚ the constant algebra is the cyclotomic determinant algebra; fixed pairing over ℚ(ζ_n) selects a component. A subgroup H descends these components by its determinant image. Identify the cusp residue fields and smoothing parameters from R13.3’s cyclotomic charts with the rational boundary points and widths in the analytic quotient. On the scalar-framed prime-p quotient, determinant classes modulo squares give exactly two complex components. No analytic comparison is used to construct X_H.

nodes.title: Compactified map comparison
nodes.statement: The compactified forgetful and quotient isogeny maps constructed algebraically agree under the generic-fibre comparison with their classical analytic degeneracy maps. On a Γ₁(N;p) chart, π₁ forgets the p-subgroup and π₂ quotients by it then contracts to the allowed level polygon. The generic analytic conventions are π₁(z)=z and π₂(z)=pz on the chosen standard branch. At every cusp compare the induced homomorphism of completed rings and the pullback of du/u. A map to a coarse curve factors by categorical universality, but finite flat stack legs do not automatically become finite flat coarse legs; descent uses the actual stabilizer action or a schematic locus where it is trivial.

nodes.title: Hecke normalization and descent
nodes.statement: On characteristic-zero fibres the geometric pull–trace correspondences agree with the earlier classical Hecke action, with the differential factor of the universal isogeny included. For weight k, the finite-flat coherent trace is pT_p, not T_p; integrality of its division by p is a separate local theorem. For Picard and étale cohomology the action is the integral push–pull of the correspondence without division by its degree. The full-subgroup A_m and cyclic C_m have their separate degrees and repeated-prime relations. These identifications descend to the field of definition with the diamond and cyclotomic Atkin–Lehner conventions fixed.

The geometric cohomological upper/lower conventions and comparison are explicit.

proofSteps: Compare the classical formula on the Tate cusp and use the imported analytic q-expansion determination.

nodes.title: Igusa components of modular fibres
nodes.statement: Over a perfect field k of characteristic p, an Igusa pʳ structure on an ordinary elliptic curve E with prescribed prime-to-p level is a Drinfeld generator of ker(Vʳ:E^(pʳ)→E). On the ordinary locus ker Vʳ is étale cyclic of rank pʳ, so its generator cover has degree φ(pʳ) before the effective residual automorphism quotient. Compactify by normalizing the corresponding level curve in this generator cover. Keep the auxiliary rigidifying level when discussing ±1 and other automorphisms; Ig(p)/±1 and Ig(p)/C₄ in Edixhoven/BDMTV denote effective quotient level problems, not two arbitrary additional quotients of an already coarse curve. Γ₀ p-power mixed components, and the middle components after the p² extension, are identified with the relevant descended Igusa problems. Smoothness, ramification at supersingular points and small-p behavior are assertions proved by the local models, not part of a definition of an ordinary cover.

Igusa is defined through Verschiebung and the middle-component quotients are specified.

nodes.title: Γ₀ prime-power local models
nodes.statement: Let p>3, n≥1 and M≥1 with p∤M. The Γ₀(pⁿM) coarse special fibre has n+1 components indexed (a,b), a+b=n, each abstractly X₀(M)_𝔽p, of multiplicity φ(p^min(a,b)). All meet at every supersingular Γ₀(M) point and nowhere else; this intersection is not claimed to be transverse for n>1. Under an étale auxiliary rigidifier the completed surface ring at a relevant noncuspidal point is W[[x,y]]/(f₀+p u), u a unit, where W=W(k̄). At a supersingular point f₀=(x^(pⁿ)−y)(x−y^(pⁿ))∏_(a+b=n,a,b>0)(x^(p^(a−1))−y^(p^(b−1)))^(p−1); on the ordinary mixed (a,b) component f₀=(x^(p^(a−1))−y^(p^(b−1)))^(p−1). These x,y are local moduli of source and target; the component-to-j maps may involve Frobenius. The all-N component/multiplicity statement extends to p=2,3 as the Katz–Mazur/Edixhoven cyclic-deformation target, but its wild invariant-ring/resolution calculation is the separate recorded gap.

nodes.title: The corrected coarse singular locus
nodes.statement: For p>3, p∤M and n≥1, a noncuspidal point of the integral Γ₀(pⁿM) coarse surface is singular exactly when its elliptic pair has automorphisms beyond ±1 and it is either supersingular or lies on a mixed (a,b) component with a,b>0. Cusps are regular. The extra automorphism condition concerns the pair (E,C_M), not just the value j=0 or 1728. Ordinary points with a=0 or b=0 are smooth over ℤ_p. This corrects the supersingular-only exception in Gross–Zagier III Proposition (1.4); no identical criterion is claimed at p=2 or 3.

nodes.title: Regular resolutions of modular fibres
nodes.statement: For p>3 and p∤M construct the minimal regular resolution of the Γ₀(pⁿM) coarse surface at p from the preceding local rings. Resolve the effective order-2/3 stabilizer action by equivariant blowups until each fixed point has pseudo-reflection cotangent action; take the tame quotient and contract the resulting exceptional −1 curves. For j=1728 the order-2 action on source/target parameters is (x,y)↦(−x,−y); one blowup yields a regular quotient with one exceptional rational curve of self-intersection −2. For j=0 supersingular and n even, the effective order-3 action has equal eigencharacters and one blowup gives one exceptional −3 curve. For j=0 supersingular and n odd, the eigencharacters are inverse; blow up the two remaining fixed points and contract the resulting −1 curve, leaving two exceptional −2 curves. Ordinary mixed points use the corresponding a>b,a=b,a<b variants. Export every component’s multiplicity and intersections by total-transform valuations and F·C=0, not just the reduced incidence graph. General blowups, intersection theory and minimal-model contractions are StableReduction’s.

nodes.statement: Let ℓ=12k+1 be prime and W=W(𝔽̄_ℓ). Over W[ϖ], ϖ^(12k(6k+1))=ℓ, X₀(ℓ²) has k horizontal curves u²=v^(ℓ+1)+1, and four vertical curves, two rational and two Ig(ℓ)/±1. Each horizontal meets each vertical once, with no other intersections. Fricke fixes each horizontal via (u,v)↦(u,−v), exchanges the rational verticals and preserves the two Igusa verticals. Its tame quotient is a proper nodal model of X_s(ℓ): k horizontals u²=v^(6k+1)+1 of genus 3k, one rational vertical and two Ig(ℓ)/C₄ verticals of genus (k−1)(3k−2)/2. Its dual graph is K_(k,3); hence b₁=2k−2 and g=6k²−3k. The chosen equation ϖ^((ℓ²−1)/2)=ℓ implies ϖ^(ℓ²−1)=ℓ². The squared equation alone also allows ϖ^((ℓ²−1)/2)=−ℓ; recover the chosen extension only with the specified root choice, not by treating the two polynomial equations as equivalent.

nodes.title: Degeneracy maps on modular components
nodes.statement: For the one-factor fine Γ₁(M)∩Γ₀(p) special fibre, identify the two components by the Frobenius and Verschiebung subgroups, retaining transported level points. With lower-level point x=(E,P), the Frobenius component has (π₁,π₂)=(id,F), where F sends (E,P) to (E^(p),P^(p)); on the Verschiebung component π₂ is the identity and π₁ is F followed by the inverse diamond transport needed to send the quotient marked point back to P. Thus the ordinary quotient sum is (E^(p),P^(p))+p(E^(p⁻¹),pP^(p⁻¹)), with the p multiplicity coming from the inseparable leg. Prime-to-level Hecke correspondences act on supersingular marked edges by quotient isogenies and their actual multiplicities; reversing the legs gives the polarization-dual action on the cycle lattice. After a coarse quotient or resolution use the induced branch and thickness maps, rather than transporting a map of sets alone.

nodes.title: Compactified Hecke degeneracy maps
nodes.statement: For N≥1 and a prime p, the disjoint Γ₁(N;p) level stack parametrizes a Γ₁(N) structure and an order-p cyclic subgroup disjoint from its marked divisor in the required generalized-curve sense. Its two maps to Γ₁(N) forget the subgroup or quotient by it and contract the polygon to restore the ample marked divisor. Both stack maps are representable finite flat over ℤ, of degree p+1 if p∤N and p if p∣N. Their universal isogeny induces ξ:π₂*ω→π₁*ω. For squarefree q use the analogous Γ₁(N;q) disjoint level problem and finite-flat legs. In characteristic zero these are the customary curve correspondences. Coarse finite flatness is asserted only after its own descent check; it does not follow just from stack finite flatness.

nodes.title: Integral étale correspondence trace
nodes.statement: For the actual finite maps f:D→C between smooth proper geometric generic-fibre modular curves and ℓ invertible in their base, use duality to define the integral H¹_et trace f_* dual to f^*. It satisfies f_*f^*=[deg f] and is compatible with Picard norm through T_ℓ Pic⁰≃H¹_et(−,ℤ_ℓ(1)). Thus π₁*π₂^* and its leg reversal give integral Hecke endomorphisms, even when ℓ divides deg π₁; no averaging is imposed. In special characteristic p≠ℓ an inseparable finite map still has its degree-weighted Gysin trace, not the sum of its distinct geometric fibres. At a bad nodal fibre use the R13.6 nearby-cycle/interface comparison; smooth-curve duality is not asserted on that singular carrier.

sources.match: The integral geometric pull–push and Picard/cup comparison fix the trace convention.

proofSteps: Import the finite-curve duality trace and prove the degree formula using the actual fundamental class.
Compare with Kummer and Picard norm, then compose the two correspondence legs.
For special nodal models use the supplied specialization exact sequence, retaining multiplicities.
acceptance: A degree-2 map with ℓ=2 has f_*f^*=[2], not identity.
Absolute Frobenius in characteristic p has degree p and its duality trace retains that factor although it is a bijection on geometric points.

nodes.title: Hecke cycles on projective level curves
nodes.statement: For prime level p>3 and m prime to p, compactify the cyclic degree-m correspondence on the scalar-framed coarse X(p) with its transported framing. For a d=m use C_(pd) as a splitting polygon: the auxiliary map φ_d:C_(pd)→C_p has smooth formula (x,c)↦(x^d,c mod p), degree d² and an isomorphism on p-torsion. For a transverse cyclic subgroup G of order d, its quotient ψ_G:C_(pd)→C_p has degree d, and ξ_a:C_p→C_p is power a on Gₘ and identity on ℤ/p. The boundary framing is ξ_a[p] ψ_G[p] φ_d[p]⁻¹ f. Retain only choices whose composite kernel is cyclic (the Tate criterion gcd(a,b,d)=1); taking every divisor a,d and every transverse G without this condition gives the full-subgroup boundary union. The source of φ_d is Gₘ×ℤ/(pd), and that of ξ_a is Gₘ×ℤ/p. Keep the μ_p-equivariance, smoothing parameter and raw/effective stabilizer distinction. For μ=id×α and ν=id×β on X(p)×T_m, the image cycle ν_*μ^*C has canonical degree ψ(m) times that of C, by projection formula and numerical equality of α^*K and β^*K. For the full-subgroup convention the multiplier is σ₁(m). This is numerical intersection equality, not a canonical line-bundle isomorphism.

sources.match: The polygon formula needs domain ℤ/(pm), and the degree multiplier depends on whether the correspondence is cyclic or full.

proofSteps: Use the split (a,d,b) Tate branch; φ_d has degree d² and is only an auxiliary p-torsion identification. The actual ξ_a ψ_G map has degree ad=m. Its kernel is cyclic exactly under the stated filter.
Transport the projective frame, retaining scalar-equivalence and stabilizers rather than introducing a nonexistent universal family.
Apply the cycle projection formula; use numerical degree on the curve, then the two equal correspondence degrees.
acceptance: m=4 gives cyclic multiplier 6, full multiplier 7.
For m=1 the cycle and canonical degree are unchanged; Γ₁ fine-level geometry is not inferred from this coarse projective statement.

nodes.title: Modular Jacobians and norms
nodes.statement: For N≥5 put S=Spec ℤ[1/N] and let C=X₁(N)/S, the smooth proper geometrically connected coarse curve. Construct J₁(N)=Pic⁰_(C/S), an abelian scheme of relative dimension g(C), with its canonical principal polarization. For X₀(N) or another smooth proper geometrically connected coarse quotient use the same construction on its legal smooth base; disconnected honest full level requires componentwise Picard and field descent. For a finite flat map f:D→C of such curves, define Picard pullback f^*:J_C→J_D and divisor norm f_*:J_D→J_C, with f_*f^*=[deg f]; the polarization dual of f^* is f_*. Norm counts the ramification/inseparable lengths, not just distinct geometric images. Under the polarization this agrees with the Albanese functor. A bad-level singular coarse fibre is not an abelian scheme: use its smooth generic Jacobian and the lower Néron model.

sources.locator: Chapter 5 §5.1, Lemma 5.4 and Definitions 5.5–5.6, pp.67–68; §5.2, pp.70–72
sources.match: Picard pullback and Albanese/norm are transpose under the canonical polarization; J₁ extends over ℤ[1/N].

proofSteps: Use the imported relative Picard representability; H² of a curve vanishes, giving smoothness via the requested lifting criterion.
Use the proper neutral-component and polarization supplier to identify the abelian scheme and its dual.
Construct norm on line bundles/divisors, checking ramification multiplicities and relative base change; prove degree and duality identities.
acceptance: For genus zero J=0, so multiplication by any degree is the unique zero endomorphism.
For a degree-2 map, norm after pullback is [2], not an identity retraction.

nodes.title: Upper and lower Jacobian Hecke operators
nodes.statement: On the generic fibre define upper T_p^J=π₁*π₂^* and lower (T_p^J)_*=π₂*π₁^*, with the same disjoint correspondence for p∣N. Define upper diamond by Picard pullback I_a^* and lower diamond by Albanese norm I_a*. Extend these endomorphisms uniquely over J₁(N)/ℤ[1/N] by normal-base Hom extension; for p∤N the degeneracy maps themselves exist on the smaller smooth base ℤ[1/Np] before this extension. The endomorphisms commute and satisfy the full-subgroup Hecke algebra relations. Their polarization transposes exchange upper/lower. On the cotangent space the lower operator is classical T_p, whereas the upper operator is its Petersson adjoint. On a bad-level Néron model extend the generic endomorphism by the Néron mapping property, without declaring its identity fibre abelian.

Compare cotangent action under Shimura and use its faithfulness in characteristic zero to transport the classical relations.

nodes.title: The geometric integral Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Define T_J as the unital image of the abstract integral full-subgroup Hecke/diamond algebra in End(J₁(N)), using the upper convention and all good/bad operators; lower gives its polarization-transpose isomorphic image. It is a commutative finite free ℤ-algebra as a ℤ-module because End(J) is finite free and T_J is a submodule. Faithful action means injectivity of this image algebra into End(J), integral Betti H¹ and End(T_ℓJ), not faithfulness of the entire abstract double-coset algebra before quotienting its kernel. Its rational rank is computed by the modular-form comparison below; on Γ₀ it equals dim_ℚ S₂(Γ₀(N),ℚ). If g=0 the image is the zero ring, of rank 0. No R14.3 eigenspace freeness or rank-two Galois theorem is used here.

nodes.title: Polarization and Hecke adjoints
nodes.statement: The canonical polarization gives a perfect alternating Weil pairing T_ℓJ×T_ℓJ→ℤ_ℓ(1). Upper and lower Hecke operators are mutually adjoint. For p∤N and upper diamond convention, T_p^†=⟨p⟩⁻¹T_p and ⟨a⟩^†=⟨a⟩⁻¹. At bad p use leg reversal, or conjugation by the chosen cyclotomic Fricke map w_ζ; do not substitute an undefined diamond p. Fricke conjugation exchanges upper/lower for all Hecke operators, so the w-twisted bilinear pairing makes the image algebra self-adjoint; this twisted pairing is not claimed alternating. After choosing ℚ̄→ℂ and roots ζ_(ℓ^r)=exp(2πi/ℓ^r), the Weil form on T_ℓPic⁰ corresponds to the negative of the integral cup form on H¹, as in Conrad’s sign convention. With Galois action retain the Tate-twist multiplier and g w_ζ g⁻¹=w_(gζ).

nodes.title: The modular Jacobian Tate module
nodes.statement: For ℓ prime, over ℚ define T_ℓJ=lim_r J[ℓ^r](ℚ̄), a finite free ℤ_ℓ-module of rank 2g with its continuous G_ℚ action and commuting rational Hecke/diamond action. Intrinsically Kummer identifies it with H¹_et(C_ℚ̄,ℤ_ℓ(1)); choosing a complex embedding and compatible roots removes the twist in the comparison with integral Betti H¹⊗ℤ_ℓ. It is not identified with H₁ without duality/polarization. The map End(J)⊗ℤ_ℓ→End_(ℤ_ℓ)(T_ℓJ) is injective with torsion-free cokernel in the supplied Hom theorem; equality with the Galois centralizer is not asserted. Good reduction over ℤ[1/N] makes this representation unramified outside Nℓ by the lower arithmetic good-reduction criterion. w_ζ is defined over its cyclotomic field and obeys semilinear Galois conjugation, rather than commuting with all G_ℚ. The module is rank 2g over ℤ_ℓ; rank 2 over a Hecke factor belongs to R14.3.

sources.match: The integral H¹/Tate comparison, commuting rational endomorphisms and unramified good-base action are the modular instance.

Apply Kummer to Pic⁰ and the supplied integral comparison, tracking the twist and sign.

At ℓ=2 the degree-2 trace remains multiplication by 2 rather than an invertible normalization.

nodes.title: The rational coefficient pairing
nodes.statement: For Γ₀(N) over ℚ identify cotangent forms with S₂(Γ₀(N),ℚ), the rational q-expansion space, using the earlier descent supplier. With the lower Jacobian Hecke image T and β(T,f)=a₁(Tf), the pairing (T⊗ℚ)×S₂(Γ₀(N),ℚ)→ℚ is perfect. The identities a_m(f)=a₁(T_m f), determination by q expansion, commutativity, and faithful cotangent action prove its two nondegeneracy statements. Consequently dim_ℚ(T⊗ℚ)=g(X₀(N)). For Γ₁ or character components, use the actual descended coefficient field and diamond action; this statement does not replace the field by ℚ without proof. Rational perfection alone does not imply an integral unimodular pairing on a chosen q-lattice.

sources.match: Faithful cotangent Hecke action and the rational a₁-pairing prove the Γ₀ rank formula.

proofSteps: If β(T,f)=0 for all T, each Fourier coefficient of f is zero, so f=0.
If β(T,f)=0 for every f, then β(T_m,Tf)=β(T_mT,f)=0 for all m,f; hence Tf=0 for every f.
Use cotangent faithfulness in characteristic zero to conclude T=0, then use finite dimension for perfection.
acceptance: Γ₀(1): both sides have dimension 0. Γ₀(11): both have dimension 1.
A determinant of an integral pairing need not be ±1 merely because its rationalization is perfect.

nodes.title: Integral Hecke realization comparison
nodes.statement: With upper/lower transpose conventions fixed, identify the same integral image of the abstract Hecke algebra on J, Betti H¹(C(ℂ),ℤ), and T_ℓJ for every ℓ. Equality of integral kernels uses the faithful Hom/Betti comparison and the supplied End⊗ℤ_ℓ injection; equality after tensoring with ℚ alone does not identify integral lattices. The additional modular-symbol comparison requires a weight-two cuspidal carrier: the kernel of the boundary map in ModularForms Layer 8’s integral symbol module, with its torsion removed, and its actual integral comparison with compact-curve H₁ (or the correctly transposed dual H¹). This missing contract is recorded as a gap; the full symbol module with boundary/Eisenstein classes is not asserted to have the same Hecke kernel. The cotangent/classical-form comparison is the lower action, and the upper action is its adjoint. Normalized coherent weight-two T_p comes from the separate local p-divisibility theorem; Jacobian/étale push–pull has no inverse-degree normalization. These compare existing Hecke actions and their image quotients, not a new abstract algebra or a rank-two eigenspace theorem.
